files.content:
codx-junior · Profile System

Presentations That Live
in a Single File

How we built the “Slides” profile — zero dependencies, keyboard-first, print-ready.

Open by naming the promise: a deck that opens offline, forever, in any browser. Set the scope — this talk is about the design of the Slides profile itself.

The problem

Today’s presentation tools are heavy

  • Slide apps demand accounts, cloud, and lock-in.
  • Design tools export — but nobody can edit the source.
  • Markdown converters work — but look like markdown.
  • Sharing means sending a link, not a file.
Four failure modes. The common thread: the artifact and the source are never the same thing. Pause after the last bullet.
01

The Idea

What if a deck were just a file?

Transition beat. One sentence: an HTML file that needs nothing else.

Principles

Five rules we locked in

  • One file, zero dependencies — opens offline, forever.
  • One idea per slide — split when in doubt.
  • Keyboard is king — never touch the mouse.
  • Print-ready — export to PDF with Cmd / Ctrl + P.
  • Narrative first, decoration last.
These are the constraints that make the rest possible. Emphasize “one file” — everything downstream depends on it.
02

The Build

What we actually shipped

Shift from concept to artifact.

Delivered

Four files, nothing to install

4
Files — 2 profile, 2 templates
12
Slide archetypes, copy-paste ready
0
External dependencies
The “0” is the headline. No CDN, no npm, no network. It just runs.

Profile anatomy

Two files make the profile

Slides.md holds the instruction manual. Slides.profile registers it and activates on .html files.

▤
Slides.md
The instruction manual
⚙
Slides.profile
Metadata + trigger (.html)
▣
templates/deck.html
Working deck shell
▦
templates/slides.html
Library of 12 archetypes
Two files define the profile; two templates are the toolkit. Walk left → right, file by file.

Architecture

The skeleton every deck shares

<!-- slides are siblings inside one deck -->
<main class="deck">
  <section class="slide active">…</section>
  <section class="slide">…</section>
  <section class="slide">…</section>
</main>

Exactly one slide carries .active. Navigation, progress, and the counter are all driven by a single render() call.

This is the invariant. Any generator that keeps this shape gets navigation for free.

Templates

Twelve slide archetypes

Cover Section Divider Agenda Bullets Two-Column Code Quote Metrics Comparison Timeline Chart Team Full Image Closing

Never invent a new layout per deck. Pick an archetype, paste it, replace the text.

The three highlighted chips are the ones every deck needs: open, prove, close. The rest are modular.

Design system

Inherited from codx-junior

  • Palette — deep canvas #0b0b0d, indigo accent #6366f1, hue = meaning.
  • Type — fluid clamp() scale, system font stack, one typeface.
  • Rhythm — 8px grid, content capped near 1100px, vertical centering.
  • Motion — a single 320ms crossfade. Nothing else.
  • Chrome — progress bar, counter, focus rings that pass WCAG AA.
The deck borrows the product’s tokens so it feels native. Restraint is the point — one accent, one grid, one typeface.

Mechanics

Navigation is ~30 lines

document.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
  if (e.key === 'ArrowRight' || e.key === ' ') next();
  if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft')  prev();
  if (e.key === 'Home')       go(0);
  if (e.key === 'End')        go(total - 1);
  if (e.key === 'f')          fullscreen();
  if (e.key === 's')          notes();
});

Plus click targets, touch swipe, and hash routing — deck.html#3 opens slide 3.

Under a hundred lines of JS total, and it covers keyboard, mouse, touch, and deep-linking. Show it live if time allows.

Workflow

Blank page to deck in four steps

01
Storyboard
List slide titles and assign an archetype to each.
02
Build
Copy the shell, paste archetypes, replace the content.
03
Validate
Tab through, resize, test fullscreen on the real display.
04
Export
Cmd / Ctrl + P → Landscape → Background graphics on.
Confirm the storyboard before writing code. Style last — always.

Thank you

One file.
Every meeting.

Open the source — or ask @Slides for the next deck.

Land the promise: the file is the deck, the deck is the file. Invite questions.
01 / 13

history.summary:
1. Requested a new **"Slides"** profile instructing how to generate HTML presentation decks.
2. Designer defined it as a **zero-dependency Presentation Architect** on the codx-junior dark-first system.
3. Delivered four files: `Slides.md` (manual), `Slides.profile` (metadata), `templates/deck.html` (shell), `templates/slides.html` (archetypes).
4. Deck shell includes keyboard/swipe/hash navigation, progress bar, speaker notes, fullscreen, and print-to-PDF CSS.
5. Library ships 12 slide archetypes: cover, divider, agenda, bullets, two-column, code, quote, metrics, comparison, timeline, chart, closing.

- Authored `Slides.md` (11-section manual) and `Slides.profile` (metadata triggering on `.html`), with the codx-junior dark-first design system baked in.
- Shipped two templates: `deck.html` (working shell with nav, progress, hash routing, notes, print CSS) and `slides.html` (12 copy-paste slide archetypes).
- Used the profile to generate a meta-deck about this very chat — 13 slides covering the problem, principles, deliverables, architecture, catalog, design system, mechanics, and workflow.
- Deliverable is one self-contained HTML file; present with arrows/Space, `F` for fullscreen, `S` for notes, and `Cmd/Ctrl + P` to export PDF.
